information_for_contributors: One grammar, many hosts: VS Code, the JetBrains TextMate bundle importer, shiki (the docs site), and any Monaco/CodeMirror build that speaks TextMate all consume this file unchanged. Edit it here and nowhere else.
TWO RULES THIS FILE MUST KEEP, both enforced by crates/ordo-syntax/tests/editor_grammar.rs:

1. `ordoInventory` below is the manifest of every word this grammar treats as vocabulary. The reserved half must equal ordo_syntax::Keyword::ALL exactly, in both directions, and be a partition. The contextual half must contain no reserved word except the ones `dual` names.

2. Every vocabulary word must be written inside a CAPTURING group in some regex — `\b(open)\b`, not `\bopen\b`. The test reads the groups; a word matched outside one is invisible to it and will be reported as absent from the grammar.

Scope names are two-layer on purpose: every leaf sits under a standard TextMate prefix (`keyword.`, `storage.modifier.`, `constant.`, `support.`), so an untuned theme colours it sensibly by prefix, while the distinctive leaf (`keyword.other.access-open.ordo`) lets an Ordo theme say something a generic theme cannot.
What this grammar deliberately CANNOT do is written down in docs/plan-editor-tooling.md, increment 0's `Known blind spots`. Do not add a rule that pretends to do one of those things.
name: Ordo

ordoInventory.comment: The manifest. See information_for_contributors. `languageVersion` is the ordo-syntax version this grammar tracks; the parity test pins it, so a language release cannot ship without the highlighter admitting which language it highlights.

comment.name: comment.line.number-sign.ordo
comment.comment: `#` to end of line, anywhere outside a string. There are no block comments — one spelling.

illegal-unterminated-string.comment: `unterminated string` and `strings do not span lines (concatenate with +)` are the same defect seen from two sides, and both are lex errors. Claimed before #string so the opening quote of a run-on string is refused rather than opening a run that dyes the rest of the file. A well-formed string never matches: the closing quote blocks the end-of-line anchor.
illegal-unterminated-string.name: invalid.illegal.unterminated-string.ordo

string.comment: A string never spans a line. The end alternative on the newline is belt-and-braces behind #illegal-unterminated-string: whatever happens, one bad quote costs one line, never the file.
string.name: string.quoted.double.ordo

patterns.comment: Typed ids live HERE and nowhere else: `_` is not an identifier character, so `task_01J8ZK…` cannot be a bare token and is only ever written inside a text literal or an id parameter's value.
patterns.name: constant.other.typed-id.ordo

patterns.comment: The closed escape set (G4): exactly these four.
patterns.name: constant.character.escape.ordo

illegal-single-quoted.comment: `No single quotes` is a settled lexical rule, so the highlighter refuses before the compiler does.
illegal-single-quoted.name: invalid.illegal.single-quoted-string.ordo

patterns.comment: `every day 08:00Z`. The Z is mandatory (§7) — and note that this whole clause is NOT one token to the lexer: `08:00Z` lexes as Int Colon Int and then a capital Z, which is a lex error. Schedules are parsed from a standalone string by ordo_syntax::trigger::Schedule. The grammar shows the settled spelling; the parser does not accept the enclosing declaration yet.
Any other schedule time: no Z, an offset, a one-digit hour. All refusals with their own messages.
`when estate.readings.created` — the event kind is a closed seven-word vocabulary, and a wildcard is legal at a whole position only.
An unrecognised kind is `unknown_event_kind`, not a pattern that silently never fires.

run-header.comment: A routine's `run(...):` header. `run` is contextual — a field may still be named `run`, so only this position colours it.

declaration-domain.comment: `domain estate @ 1.0.0`. The version is one visual thing and three tokens: the lexer sees Decimal(`1.0`), Dot, Int(`0`) and declparse::version_text reassembles them. Colouring it whole is the honest rendering of what the author wrote.

declaration-routine.comment: `routine leaseExpiry in estate {`. `in` is the boolean-membership operator everywhere else in the language; here it is a clause word, and only this position can tell.

declaration-bare.comment: The same heads with no name after them, so an in-progress line still colours.

access.comment: A guard clause runs to end of line — UNLESS a delimiter is open, which is G6 stated as a grammar rule: while #parens is on the stack this rule's `end` is never tested, so a guard wrapped inside its parens stays one clause across lines, exactly as the lexer treats it. Inside the clause `open` means the decision to open, and `$caller` is the anchor the whole guard grammar exists to reach.

group-reduce.comment: Aggregate names are contextual — `count` is a legal field name — so they are coloured as functions only inside a group/reduce brace block, and only in the value position (`n: count`, never a key named `count:`).

patterns.comment: `$caller` is the one reserved parameter (never client-suppliable) and `$trigger` is the listener envelope. Both are platform-supplied, so both read as language, not as an author's parameter.
patterns.name: variable.language.ordo

patterns.comment: `a parameter is $ followed by a lowercase name`.
patterns.name: invalid.illegal.parameter.ordo

patterns.comment: Datetime: UTC only, the Z is mandatory.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.datetime.ordo

patterns.comment: A date literal must name a day that exists. A regex can carry the month lengths, so 2026-02-31, 2026-04-31 and 2026-11-31 are refused here exactly as the lexer refuses them. It cannot carry the leap rule: 2026-02-29 needs arithmetic on the year, so it is coloured as a valid date and the compiler is the one that refuses it. That is the honest split, and it is the ONLY calendar case this file gets wrong on purpose.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.date.ordo

patterns.comment: `90d`, `1mo`, `500ms`, `5m` — `m` is minutes and `mo` is months, spelling and never context.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.duration.ordo

patterns.comment: `unknown duration unit — units are ms s m h d w mo y`.
patterns.name: invalid.illegal.duration-unit.ordo

patterns.comment: Exact decimal. No float exists anywhere in this language.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.decimal.ordo

ref-declaration.comment: `property -> properties owned`. Anchored at line start because `->` also means `yields` in cond arms, in `each ->` and in a trigger's `-> run`, and only position tells them apart. A shape's refs are always the line.

field-declaration.comment: The name in `name:` — a shape field, a write payload key, an aggregate output. All of them are a name being bound, which is one thing and gets one colour. The colon is left unconsumed so #type can claim it.

allocate.comment: The blessed money split. Its optional third argument names WHICH party absorbs the odd minor unit — a business rule, from a closed set, and an unknown mode is a compile error rather than a silent default. It is coloured only inside allocate's own parens, because `last` is an ordinary field name anywhere else.

function.comment: The closed expression-function set, with its arities checked by the parser. Coloured only when a `(` follows, so a field named `round` stays a field.

keywords.comment: The reserved tier, split by what a word DOES rather than by one flat `keyword` colour: a theme that wants declarations loud and word-operators quiet can have it, and `unguarded` — the one word in the language that switches authorization off — has a scope of its very own so it can be made impossible to skim past.

illegal-name.comment: One identifier rule for every declared name: lowerCamel, no underscores, no hyphens, 64 characters. The lexer's three refusals, shown before the compiler runs. The hyphen case is absent on purpose — `lease-expiry` is genuinely `lease` minus `expiry` and no regex can know which was meant.

patterns.comment: `!` is not an operator — negation is the word `not`, inequality is `!=`.
patterns.name: invalid.illegal.operator.ordo

patterns.comment: The pipeline bar: a filter step whose scope is decided by where it sits.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.bar.ordo
